reader.notes: The generated __IoCheck returns before selecting a declarative when __invKey is set and the status is 2x. EmitPhrasePair renders the INVALID KEY body as if (2x) followed by else-if (0x) for NOT INVALID KEY, so an explicit transfer leaves through ordinary C# control flow. The same code runs at every edition.

refuter.evidence: Probe r2_global.cob at --std 85 (runs/r2_global-001). A 1985 level-2 IPC form the reader did not try: USE GLOBAL AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION in the containing program on a GLOBAL relative FD, with the I-O in a contained program. A WRITE duplicate with INVALID KEY gives IN-IK-WD 22 and a READ absent with INVALID KEY gives IN-IK-R9 23, and in neither case does GUSE-RX or a NOT INVALID KEY line print. A READ RY on a file not open, nested inside the INVALID KEY imperative, still runs the GLOBAL USE (GUSE-RY 47), then the imperative continues (IN-IK-R8-END 23 47) to the end of the statement, so suppression is per statement. cite.py: OK §1985:VIII.1.3.5 GR2 the text is in GR2. Minor missed edition site: DispatchEmitter.cs line 523 (DialectLevel >= 2002) changes only the SORT GR17 exit filter around a declarative's run, not the invalid-key path.
